solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicatorNotes.used in: TOO is put to use inside the strategy word

blocks.note: a plan = a strategy
too = also

annotation.surface: An officer explains that troops also have a part in the battle plan.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is so military that "strategy" feels like more of the definition, but it is only a building block.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small army unit, made up of a few sections of soldiers.

blocks.note: POW = prisoner of war
both are exclamations of surprise

annotation.surface: Someone is startled to be introduced to a prisoner.
annotation.walkthrough: "I say" is an old British exclamation of surprise, so it can stand for WOW.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, borrowed from a Native American word for a council or gathering.

entries.clue: When Panama falls for no good reason (2,3,4,2,1,3)

annotation.answer: AT THE DROP OF A HAT

blocks.note: a Panama is a straw hat, so this is the moment it drops
the idiom: on the slightest excuse

annotation.surface: A news line about the fall of a Central American country, apparently for no reason.
annotation.walkthrough: Panama looks like the country, but here it is the straw hat, so the first half is read literally.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for acting readily on the slightest excuse, and read literally it is the moment a hat falls.

blocks.note: a slip, something missed through not looking
supervision, watching over a task

annotation.surface: A complaint that the bosses have let things go wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The one word carries two nearly opposite senses: missing something, and watching over it.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: the same word means both a lapse in attention and supervision.

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, lifting a word makes it read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes above it

blocks.note: a son is a boy
H = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A child brought up on spicy meals.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang, from Yiddish, for something to eat.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British English: a slang word for grub or a meal.

indicatorNotes.corrupted: a corrupted file has its letters scrambled
indicatorNotes.in: the scrambled letters go inside the computer word

blocks.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
FILE rearranged

annotation.surface: A damaged file on a computer turns out to be malicious.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is pure computing, and "corrupted" is the anagram signal that fits it so well you hardly notice it.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary synonym for evil or hurtful, from the Latin for doing wrong.

indicatorNotes.across: the lawgiver is stretched across the capital, on both sides of it

blocks.note: Moses brought the Ten Commandments
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

annotation.surface: A legislator takes a flight across the country to the capital.
annotation.walkthrough: "Flies" reads as a verb, with the lawgiver taking a plane, but it is a plural noun: the insects.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: these biting insects have two wings, so they belong to the true flies.

blocks.note: the late X = the dead X
R = right

annotation.surface: A question about putting something off, answered with a firm yes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dead right" looks like one phrase meaning exactly right, but it splits into two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: The question mark marks a definition by description: some time other than the present.

entries.clue: A drawing that’s disastrous as a picture (5,10)

blocks.note: fatal = disastrous
attraction = drawing, as in drawing a crowd

annotation.surface: An art critic pans a drawing as a dreadful picture.
annotation.walkthrough: Drawing and picture both sound like art, but the drawing is a pull and the picture is a film.
annotation.definitionFit: Picture is the old word for a film, and this is the 1987 thriller with Michael Douglas and Glenn Close.

indicatorNotes.off: the letters of NOD go off, out of order

blocks.note: the punctuation mark in the clue itself
NOD rearranged

annotation.surface: An order to a soldier on sentry duty: fall asleep.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after "Soldier" looks like plain punctuation, but it is a word in the wordplay. "Nod off" looks like dozing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a member of a special unit trained for raids is a kind of soldier.

indicatorNotes.upset: the letters of SENSES are knocked over into a new order

blocks.note: a wit is a funny person
SENSES rearranged

annotation.surface: A stand-up senses that the audience is offended.
annotation.walkthrough: "Upset viewers" looks like offended people, but "upset" goes back to scramble "senses".
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people who see an event happen, as in a court case.

blocks.note: to tote is to carry, or bear
M = male

annotation.surface: A male bear treated as holy, like an animal spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bear" looks like the animal, which is common on carved poles, but here it is the verb to carry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an object or animal revered as the emblem of a clan.

entries.clue: Port behind old Tokyo, to the west (6)

indicatorNotes.to the west: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

blocks.note: ass = behind, the backside
Edo was Tokyo's old name

annotation.surface: Directions to a harbour behind the old city of Tokyo, on its west side.
annotation.walkthrough: "Behind" reads as a position word, but it is a noun, the backside.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a Black Sea harbour city in Ukraine.

indicatorNotes.Utter: to utter is to speak, so the answer is how the brute's name is said

blocks.note: a gorilla is a big brute

annotation.surface: An insult: a complete brute stands in for a boxer.
annotation.walkthrough: "Utter" looks like the adjective "complete", but here it is the verb to say.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an irregular soldier in a small independent band.

entries.clue: Trifle that’s sweet, more or less (4,6)

blocks.note: a fool is a British fruit and cream pudding
around = roughly, more or less

annotation.surface: A description of a trifle pudding, which is sort of sweet.
annotation.walkthrough: Trifle and sweet both look like puddings, but "Trifle" is the verb to mess about. A fool is a British dessert of fruit and cream.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb sense of trifle: to mess about, treating something without seriousness.

indicatorNotes.sports: the letters play around, like athletes

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: Someone who watches games does exactly as the pundits predicted.
annotation.walkthrough: "Spectator sports" reads as one phrase, but the fodder ends at "spectator" and "sports" is the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both past tense verbs: predicted what would happen.

entries.clue: Plant fibre thus gets new twigs (7,2)

blocks.note: cotton is a plant fibre
so = thus
N = new

annotation.surface: A gardening note: the cotton plant is putting out new shoots.
annotation.walkthrough: "Twigs" looks like small branches, but it is British slang for understands.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are British slang verbs for realising or catching on.

entries.clue: Last part of Aida polished off, get going (8)

blocks.note: Verdi's Aida has four acts, so its last is Act IV
to polish off food is to eat it

annotation.surface: An opera-goer, the final act over, is told to leave.
annotation.walkthrough: "Last part" looks like an instruction to take the last letter, A, but the part is an act of the opera.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to set something working or start it up.

blocks.note: the letter A written big, in the plural
the learning of a capital city, Paris

annotation.surface: A question asking whether French culture is one example of something.
annotation.walkthrough: The big A of "As" is the clue: it is the plural of the letter A, not the word as. Letters here means learning, as in a man of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Big As are an example of the first sense, and the letters (learning) of a capital city like Paris is the playful second.

entries.clue: Not even fish will swallow goods (6)

indicatorNotes.will swallow: the fish takes the goods inside it

blocks.note: a cray is a crayfish
G = good, so two of them

annotation.surface: Even a fish refuses to eat the product.
annotation.walkthrough: "Not even" looks like "not so much as", but it means uneven, rough.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rugged and uneven, like a rock face.

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, the lines are placed on, after, the child

blocks.note: an infant is a young child
RY = railway, a set of lines

annotation.surface: Wrinkles or marks on a small child's foot.
annotation.walkthrough: "Foot" looks like the body part, but it is the foot soldiers of an army.
annotation.definitionFit: Foot is short for foot soldiers, the troops who march rather than ride.

indicatorNotes.In: the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: kindergarteN A DIRty

annotation.surface: A small child at nursery school with a muddy backside.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bottom" looks like a child's backside, but it is the lowest point.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the lowest point of anything, from astronomy's point directly below the observer.

entries.clue: Football’s big hitter on the radio (6)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: on the radio, you hear the words rather than see them

blocks.note: to sock is to hit hard, so a socker is a hitter

annotation.surface: A radio commentator talking about football's star player.
annotation.walkthrough: "Big hitter" suggests an important person, but it is someone who socks, or punches.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word is a shortening of association football.

indicatorNotes.Not: tells you to leave out the very

blocks.note: to vomit is to be sick
V = very, removed

annotation.surface: A young woman asks if she is ill and is told: not much.
annotation.walkthrough: "Miss" looks like a young woman, but it is the verb to leave out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to leave something out or undone.

blocks.note: AP = Associated Press
to hide is not to disclose

annotation.surface: A news agency kept a secret about a listening device.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bug" looks like a hidden microphone, which suits the secretive surface, but it is an insect.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a small sap-sucking insect, such as a greenfly.

entries.clue: Showing off, gunman’s about to go downhill (9)

indicatorNotes.off: the gunman's letters go off, out of order
indicatorNotes.’s about: the rearranged gunman is around the next piece

blocks.note: GUNMAN rearranged
to ski is to go downhill

annotation.surface: A gunman is about to set off down a slope, showing off.
annotation.walkthrough: "Showing off" looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at "Showing" and "off" goes with the gunman.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: revealing what was hidden, as in taking a disguise away.

blocks.note: the surface reads this as seemed; the setter means came on stage
the surface reads this as to take action; the setter means to perform a role

annotation.surface: Someone only pretended to do something.
annotation.walkthrough: "Appeared to act" reads as "seemed to act", but it means came on stage to perform.
annotation.definitionFit: An actor walking on stage to perform makes an entrance, the stage sense of the answer.

indicatorNotes.evacuated: the word is emptied of its middle, leaving the ends

blocks.note: ThE with its middle removed
Nancy is a city in north-east France

annotation.surface: A French city is being held after its people have fled.
annotation.walkthrough: "Evacuated" suggests a city cleared of people, but it empties the word "the".
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: occupying land or property as a tenant.
